items.narrative:
This audit covers a 3-day window from 2026-06-10 to 2026-06-12, during which 3 supply-chain events were recorded across receiving, shipping, and transformation critical tracking events. Of the 2 products in scope, 1 is definitively on the Food Traceability List and 1 is classified as suspicious, meaning its FTL status has not been resolved. No external trading partners were identified, yet 2 events logged an unknown destination, leaving the full trading-partner picture incomplete.

The operation carries 6 findings in total — 2 rated high severity and 4 rated medium. The two high-severity findings fall across tlc_lineage (2 findings combined) and the remaining medium findings span traceability_plan, kde_completeness, partner_data_quality, and exemption_claim categories. Key data element coverage sits at 0.7407, meaning 7 of 27 graded KDE slots are missing outright, and the traceability plan itself has a recorded deficiency, which is a foundational compliance gap. The suspicious product's unresolved FTL classification compounds risk because any obligation to maintain full lot-level records cannot be confirmed or dismissed until that determination is made.

Immediately resolve the FTL classification for the 1 suspicious product — document the determination in writing before any further shipments occur. Address the 2 tlc_lineage findings next, as these are the highest-severity gaps and directly undermine lot-level backward traceability; only 1 backward lineage link is currently confirmed. Fill the 7 missing KDE values identified in the kde_completeness finding, correct the traceability plan deficiency, and investigate the 2 events with unknown destinations to assign proper receiving-party records. The exemption_claim and partner_data_quality findings should be resolved concurrently but can follow the lot-lineage and KDE remediation work.
